deep.reconstruction: This page contains no mathematics. It is a short handwritten public notice (Anschlag) announcing the start of a lecture course. In translation: 'I intend to begin my lectures on the theory of partial differential equations on Tuesday the 29th of April in Auditorium No. 14. Göttingen, the 26th of April 1862. B. Riemann.' It belongs to the summer semester 1862 at Göttingen. Riemann's lecture course on partial differential equations and their application to physical problems was later edited by K. Hattendorff ('Partielle Differentialgleichungen und deren Anwendung auf physikalische Fragen', 1869), drawing on Riemann's lectures of around 1860-1862. The notice dates one of these courses precisely. The course was given shortly before Riemann's marriage (June 1862) and his serious illness in the autumn of 1862. The neighbouring pages are unrelated: the previous one is a printed Berlin university lecture index, and the next has scattered formulas on log((z+ai)/(z-ai)) and a substitution integral. They do not bear on this notice. There is nothing to reconstruct mathematically.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors. The internal date consistency checks out (my verification): 29 April 1862 was indeed a Tuesday (Dienstag), and 26 April 1862 was a Saturday.

results.what: Announcement of Riemann's lecture course on the theory of partial differential equations, to begin Tuesday 29 April 1862, Auditorium No. 14, Göttingen (summer semester 1862).
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (the PDE lectures are known through Hattendorff's 1869 edition)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine administrative notice. It is a minor archival datum confirming the exact start date and room of a lecture course that Riemann is already known to have given. There is no mathematical content.

checkable.asserts: 29 April 1862 was a Tuesday (Monday=0), consistent with 'Dienstag den 29. April'.
The notice was dated Saturday 26 April 1862, three days before the lecture start.

transcription_corrections: The transcription is essentially correct. The signature reads 'B. Riemann.' (the Kurrent B can resemble an L or other letter, but B is correct). The text is in German Kurrent script: 'Meine Vorlesungen über die Theorie der partiellen Differentialgleichungen gedenke ich am Dienstag den 29. April im Auditorium № 14 zu beginnen'.
The pencilled '63' at the right margin is the archival folio number, not part of Riemann's text.
